context.title: Hearing the Word
context.summary: Women support Jesus' mission. He tells the parable of the sower and the lamp, calms a storm, frees the demon-possessed man of the Gadarenes, heals a bleeding woman and raises Jairus' daughter.
context.background: Luke names women who traveled with Jesus and funded his work from their own means, including Joanna, wife of a manager in Herod's household (vv. 2–3). Women supporting a teacher this openly was unusual, and Luke highlights it.

customs.note: Under the law, ongoing bleeding made a woman ritually unclean and passed that status to what she touched (Leviticus 15:25-27). Her touch does not defile Jesus; she is healed.

watchFor: Jesus defines his family as those who 'hear the word of God, and do it' (v. 21).

people.name: Mary
people.summary: A surname derived from Magdala, the place of her nativity, given to one of the Marys of the Gospels to distinguish her from the other Marys (Matt. 27:56, 61; 28:1, etc.).

people.name: Heber
people.summary: Son of Beriah and grandson of Asher (Gen. 46:17; 1 Chr. 7:31, 32).

people.name: Joanna
people.summary: The wife of Chuza, the steward of Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee (Luke 8:3).

people.name: Susanna
people.summary: Lily, with other pious women, ministered to Jesus (Luke 8:3).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Jairus
people.summary: A ruler of the synagogue at Capernaum, whose only daughter Jesus restored to life (Mark 5:22; Luke 8:41).

people.name: Simon
people.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture.

people.name: John
people.summary: THE APOSTLE, brother of James the “Greater” (Matt. 4:21; 10:2; Mark 1:19; 3:17; 10:35). He was one, probably the younger, of the sons of Zebedee (Matt. 4:21) and Salome (Matt. 27:56; comp. Mark 15:40), and was born at Bethsaida.

people.name: James
people.summary: The son of Zebedee and Salome; an elder brother of John the apostle. He was one of the twelve. He was by trade a fisherman, in partnership with Peter (Matt. 20:20; 27:56).

places.name: Galilee
places.summary: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul”.
